body.statement: For rational or algebraic primitive inputs, finite unions of closed rational intervals presenting each projected alternative coordinate, and every rational tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), the handle in \(\mathrm{def{:}tolerance\mbox{-}handle}\) terminates with an interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\) containing the full-cell conditional value \(V^{\star}\), a finite outer union containing \(\mathcal{S}^{\star}\) and contained in the \(2\varepsilon\)-power superlevel set, and a finite inner union contained in the \(\varepsilon\)-power superlevel set. It asserts a unique design only when the supplied separation certificate proves uniqueness against every retained competing branch and slack-cell weight set.
body.justification: The computational statement is strong enough for design use but never asks an interval routine to decide equality of arbitrary exact real values.
body.gap: Published enrichment optimizers report numerical solutions without a theorem enclosing the full optimizer set across equality strata.
body.consumer: A protocol can archive machine-checkable value and design boxes and reserve point recommendations for explicitly separated cases.
body.proof_tex:
For algebraic or rational inputs, \(\phi\), \(\Phi\), and their derivatives have terminating outward rational enclosures on compact intervals by their power series together with standard Gaussian tail bounds. The residual-scale lemma supplies \(v\ge\sqrt{\rho_0}>0\). Choose a finite rational \(M\) so that the unconditional Gaussian tails outside \([-M,M]\) are smaller than the fixed conditional-tail margins. Then every null critical value lies in \([-M,M]\). On this compact set the derivative of the defining tail probability with respect to \(q\) is a continuous strictly negative Gaussian density and hence has an effectively positive lower enclosure. Bisection with outward tail integration therefore terminates for every requested critical-value accuracy. Differentiating the integral on the enlarged compact domain supplies an effective common oscillation bound for every \(\Pi_j\), and hence for the finite minimum objective
\[
\Psi(\rho,\theta)=\min_{j\in J}\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s).
\]

Fix rational \(\varepsilon>0\). Subdivide the compact design domain into finitely many rational boxes until interval evaluation supplies an enclosure \([L_B,U_B]\) of \(\Psi\) on every box with \(U_B-L_B\le\delta\), where \(0<\delta\le\varepsilon\). Set \(L^\star=\max_B L_B\) and \(U^\star=\max_B U_B\). A box containing an optimizer shows \(L^\star\le V^\star\le U^\star\), and \(U_B\le L_B+\delta\le L^\star+\delta\) for every \(B\), so \(U^\star-L^\star\le\delta\le\varepsilon\).

Retain in the outer union every box with \(U_B\ge L^\star\). Every optimizer box is retained. For any retained box and every point in it,
\[
\Psi\ge L_B\ge U_B-\delta\ge L^\star-\delta\ge V^\star-2\delta\ge V^\star-2\varepsilon.
\]
Thus the outer union is contained in the \(2\varepsilon\)-power superlevel set. Any boxes satisfying \(L_B\ge U^\star-\varepsilon\) form a finite inner union, possibly empty, on which \(\Psi\ge V^\star-\varepsilon\). Every comparison is between rational interval endpoints, so equality of arbitrary exact reals is never queried.

Finally, a supplied separation certificate is checked by interval root existence and uniqueness on its isolating boxes, exclusion bounds on their complements, strict interval comparisons of all competing branch values, and a positive objective gap outside the winning neighborhoods. If all checks pass, the branch characterization excludes every other optimizer and refinement yields arbitrarily small boxes around the unique design. Without those checks, the algorithm reports only the value and set enclosures just proved and makes no uniqueness assertion.
